E3A7192994924D638DD82B5C02E8E1A9.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

B3D006E46D2A41618DBBC08D26FBBB1E.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

E112C3AC80034EE8B494C03D1A7EF9BB.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

F65AB78AEF35470DB29645C457C7FB6D.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

1761C4951F2549948E8E6C5578358DF5.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

E09E546512CB4069A901ABCC422A955A.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

4A47E447D74940B3AAAD02A7B0A51EEC.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

29432ADBF9A748DE91629E942AFEDFD7.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

D3188801C3EB4016A06028C9026857AA.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.

DB1B86EDEE464D8F9194AD60D63F9147.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

3ABD890FF2424BD498841D4EB876CE0F.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

3629FEC0E415492B83A519B346670FE3.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. EB6727730B60495396B05E30E74FDF1D.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

785869D1B7B24952977410C393B7D035.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

38FF105875624E98966EBF0A687453B4.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

9DDD6751EECA46F19F02C41C76F6F334.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

149DFE9612EB40999EAA516CB9B14B6E.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.

A7927F17C6C34442B268C31E44F88EF7.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. 36EC275A59584B4B9D3206465793A00F.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.

1CA47B248B0A4E1E9298DB0AA9123EA9.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

B8DE11D6D3E349679F776B1D486C71CA.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

3B9FE88C99874D8696F12290153C2156.description: Look for and make use of structure.

373DD07DF4F3494188AE992E0C3593E9.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

2EB62DCB293545D48232E4DDEF0BFD12.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Carolina Standard Course of Study K-8 Mathematics

46CCEE1FEADB4264B126C21827209677.description:
Qualitatively analyze the functional relationship between two quantities.
  • Analyze a graph determining where the function is increasing or decreasing; linear or non-linear.
  • Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a real-world function.

EC1A3CE11B444FD0B5DB16FF061E0A98.description:
Analyze functions that model linear relationships.
  • Understand that a linear relationship can be generalized by y = mx + b.
  • Write an equation in slope-intercept form to model a linear relationship by determining the rate of change and the initial value, given at least two (x, y) values or a graph.
  • Construct a graph of a linear relationship given an equation in slope-intercept form.
  • Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of the slope and y-intercept of its graph or a table of values.

893DAD059CCE4D0FBADC889165F5B94B.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

3E2DFEAEE4EA43F6B7ABFEAA771AFA44.description: Identify linear functions from tables, equations, and graphs.

6F319B2BAE12427F914E9E93A093FA3E.description: Compare properties of two linear functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

8979034BE3FC463EA4C5F5869E3B7366.description:
Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output.
  • Recognize functions when graphed as the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and exactly one corresponding output.
  • Recognize functions given a table of values or a set of ordered pairs.

A494B524A3144109BC9E57DEB5845248.description:
Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table.
  • Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects.
  • Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.

9C06A4BA97A142C89583D4BB2DFD7E98.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate quantitative data, interpreting the slope and y-intercept.

2A296053EE844C7A9CC628A4D1CB62BB.description:
Model the relationship between bivariate quantitative data to:
  • Informally fit a straight line for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.
  • Informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

F50A8E78281F4A0299FEBE225595CCAF.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Investigate and describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

F4BC8A0589CF416EAF8F2400A327E5A2.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

7D91400ACB9447E5B2F8A48109E0EF4D.description:
Analyze and solve a system of two linear equations in two variables in slope-intercept form.
  • Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations correspond to the points of intersection of their graphs because the point of intersection satisfies both equations simultaneously.
  • Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to systems of linear equations by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.

0F4F65F12FF54EBB84B8959113FB42F5.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

7C8FECCED64B4E079E0FC2EFBE61C782.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations and inequalities in one variable.
  • Recognize linear equations in one variable as having one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions.
  • Solve linear equations and inequalities including multi-step equations and inequalities with the same variable on both sides.

BBBD531DE1FF47E680254B3A8D4E8F08.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and inequalities.

8854BDC978704ECF97EABB6B984795E6.description: Perform multiplication and division with numbers expressed in scientific notation to solve real-world problems, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used.

BE255BD0661D46E19C1D41118E2D85C7.description: Use numbers expressed in scientific notation to estimate very large or very small quantities and to express how many times as much one is than the other.

F2165DEEA6F6428D969F34FC96D4F702.description:
Use square root and cube root symbols to:
  • Represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ =p, where p is a positive rational number.
  • Evaluate square roots of perfect squares and cube roots of perfect cubes for positive numbers less than or equal to 400.

9B94EE5877A446B9AFA0EF01AB61BA68.description: Develop and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

881864C4993C497ABE5DFC648ED6EF66.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

F4F986C16EF14194BCD81EE6CAA3CFC4.description:
Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers and locate them approximately on a number line. Estimate the value of expressions involving:
  • Square roots and cube roots to the tenths.
  • π to the hundredths.

B0B3C5E047F641389DD19EFECF493E62.description: Understand that every number has a decimal expansion. Building upon the definition of a rational number, know that an irrational number is defined as a non-repeating, non-terminating decimal.

9392EEC0B70C4115AAA252E8AAE6F9A8.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

A6236DDB369844909870363594CDC82F.description: Understand how the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres are related and use the relationship to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

BA7A78B759F443558854164776745E72.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

951FE175B8B344CD891DC223E225FC38.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

AD883E200E934D2ABCE5C00253289103.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

9F641A0F40C341078AD6274E22D4221B.description: Explain the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

DF6A8290DCB141A697797867F8548391.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

F97E02E367554C4E80BE70DAC678E230.description:
Use informal arguments to analyze angle relationships.
  • Recognize relationships between interior and exterior angles of a triangle.
  • Recognize the relationships between the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal.
  • Recognize the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.
  • Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving angles.

5E410F6066274A2FAD2140CE156130D9.description:
Use transformations to define similarity.
  • Verify experimentally the properties of dilations that create similar figures.
  • Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations.
  • Given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

B2EA2C2BB808483493A51DE638A21D8D.description: Describe the effect of dilations about the origin, translations, rotations about the origin in 90 degree increments, and reflections across the x-axis and y-axis on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

D967FBCA92D045FB84A687FEA5F2E194.description:
Use transformations to define congruence.
  • Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations that create congruent figures.
  • Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations.
  • Given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

7B259EE6BD1B40F5BC7472DE164F3C86.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

A774C6D49975492C8A6E65BFEE86AAFE.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

9CB2656F2D1F4A7E9E6FB48C5AFA5E8B.description: Look for and make use of structure.

A6CA1F640CB14824915F90C503FDF28C.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

86BACD518E8E48DF9E7E09697122BD15.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Carolina Standard Course of Study K-8 Mathematics

60CB56F5281E42E89E849FE163B6D426.description: Solve one-step word problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions using area and length models, and equations to represent the problem.

97E708AD7B1148F7ADE2F6BEC2DB0FCF.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction, including mixed numbers.
  • Use area and length models to multiply two fractions, with the denominators 2, 3, 4.
  • Explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number and when multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number.
  • Solve one-step word problems involving multiplication of fractions using models to develop the algorithm.

06D3C445CA2944FB983238A735D7821B.description:
Use fractions to model and solve division problems.
  • Interpret a fraction as an equal sharing context, where a quantity is divided into equal parts.
  • Model and interpret a fraction as the division of the numerator by the denominator.
  • Solve one-step word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions and mixed numbers, with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12, using area, length, and set models or equations.

B0C9990AFF6349DC9FCF970AF5F19083.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

B753D8FA99FA459CBA5B6C2BB3C04CE4.description:
Add and subtract fractions, including mixed numbers, with unlike denominators using related fractions: halves, fourths and eighths; thirds, sixths, and twelfths; fifths, tenths, and hundredths.
  • Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.
  • Solve one- and two-step word problems in context using area and length models to develop the algorithm. Represent the word problem in an equation.

3FB30FE043A34085821D3809735D90B4.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

88DF1BA245A14BEF9138CD62EE66B575.description:
Classify quadrilaterals into categories based on their properties.
  • Explain that attributes belonging to a category of quadrilaterals also belong to all subcategories of that category.
  • Classify quadrilaterals in a hierarchy based on properties.

D39DFFC0453C4B02A1D510971E66ECCD.description: Graph points in the first quadrant of a coordinate plane, and identify and interpret the x and y coordinates to solve problems.

3F136861C11A4A49926866FAB491B14E.description:
Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition.
  • Find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths.
  • Build understanding of the volume formula for rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving problems.
  • Find volume of solid figures with one-digit dimensions composed of two non-overlapping rectangular prisms.

C1DE481F234C4669B2A99E9DA4ED75A3.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and measure volume by counting unit cubes, using cubic centimeters, cubic inches, cubic feet, and improvised units.

7BF5AD579FED441EBD6449853F8AB52D.description: Given a conversion chart, use multiplicative reasoning to solve one-step conversion problems within a given measurement system.

8C9B23EAC955400294EE726635217CCC.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

F5834CBAEF8341A7BF7CEBD42A5CEE94.description:
Represent and interpret data.
  • Collect data by asking a question that yields data that changes over time.
  • Make and interpret a representation of data using a line graph.
  • Determine whether a survey question will yield categorical or numerical data, or data that changes over time.

84D39CBA623749DC847EEC1D2227937B.description:
Compute and solve real-world problems with multi-digit whole numbers and decimal numbers.
  • Add and subtract decimals to thousandths using models, drawings or strategies based on place value.
  • Multiply decimals with a product to thousandths using models, drawings, or strategies based on place value.
  • Divide a whole number by a decimal and divide a decimal by a whole number, using repeated subtraction or area models.
Decimals should be limited to hundredths.
  • Use estimation strategies to assess reasonableness of answers.

C3CF5BE1A86C41F9A85C348B95FC8CDF.description: Find quotients with remainders when dividing whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors using rectangular arrays, area models, repeated subtraction, partial quotients, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Use models to make connections and develop the algorithm.

B2A5ADA666394174BBCDAA1F6F71CC65.description: Demonstrate fluency with the multiplication of two whole numbers up to a three-digit number by a two-digit number using the standard algorithm.

76FC2BDFE7DF44B7961B684D3286682C.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers.

332433C92C294C1084E1CC547947C851.description:
Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.
  • Write decimals using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
  • Compare two decimals to thousandths based on the value of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

63E8399249854251B8A817499F414EAF.description:
Explain the patterns in the place value system from one million to the thousandths place.
  • Explain that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.
  • Explain patterns in products and quotients when numbers are multiplied by 1,000, 100, 10, 0.1, and 0.01 and/or divided by 10 and 100.

172F5D56471D49DA8888AFBB518F7FF6.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

8EF7DDABB5164CCA95CDC9B03B5F4498.description:
Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules.
  • Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms.
  • Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns.
  • Graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

2CBCEA1373EF4F29B15DB5BFE61D989B.description:
Write, explain, and evaluate numerical expressions involving the four operations to solve up to two-step problems. Include expressions involving:
  • Parentheses, using the order of operations.
  • Commutative, associative and distributive properties.

D78E530B62CA4E339C89B4C296C82D6F.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

0CF118BBAB8046DEB525E31A7F7BA92E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

302C8EB6BD474B97B7FAD6843A050CAD.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

73A94870E3424DF6AD57AC7C8BBF05AA.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Carolina Standard Course of Study K-8 Mathematics

DB3628102D6F4107B6F8A2274E9CB8CB.description:
Analyze center and variability by:
  • Giving quantitative measures of center, describing variability, and any overall pattern, and noting any striking deviations.
  • Justifying the appropriate choice of measures of center using the shape of the data distribution.

DCF4ECDACE5143A39F2B910570908B7F.description:
Describe the collected data by:
  • Reporting the number of observations in dot plots and histograms.
  • Communicating the nature of the attribute under investigation, how it was measured, and the units of measurement.

72435CF416CC47BAB1E2918B0F73A80A.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.

F87E038D0BC8492E8F16AEC8498F146F.description:
Display numerical data in plots on a number line.
  • Use dot plots, histograms, and box plots to represent data.
  • Compare the attributes of different representations of the same data.

0A230A9BE5704515AC0CFFF395B18D42.description: Understand that describing the variability of a data set is needed to distinguish between data sets in the same scale, by comparing graphical representations of different data sets in the same scale that have similar measures of center, but different spreads.

27CC500166744D90A5943B82063B99DF.description:
Determine the measure of center of a data set and understand that it is a single number that summarizes all the values of that data set.
  • Understand that a mean is a measure of center that represents a balance point or fair share of a data set and can be influenced by the presence of extreme values within the data set.
  • Understand the median as a measure of center that is the numerical middle of an ordered data set.

52BC8D03C1AE499AA22B32F590CAAC25.description: Understand that both a measure of center and a description of variability should be considered when describing a numerical data set.

C0ED48D9E2F1402A9FA89084AA970595.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

B150BBCBFD1F488EA6CC7BF2B756E191.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

EF3E216EBBA6471C8C78734150763BEB.description: Represent right prisms and right pyramids using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

7009A5EC35B743A1937233D4123FE9E6.description:
Use the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems by:
  • Drawing polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices.
  • Using coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

7E31BAC463C3468599BD843973CE7ECC.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of the volume of a right rectangular prism to find the volume of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths. Apply this understanding to the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

F7458FFB6E3D4E7D993C33652B12C80D.description:
Create geometric models to solve real-world and mathematical problems to:
  • Find the area of triangles by composing into rectangles and decomposing into right triangles.
  • Find the area of special quadrilaterals and polygons by decomposing into triangles or rectangles.

9E215A3FE83340FF8EFD614A9E2B0CE3.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

58D499E9A56E4C83A377AB8CA9B4E8EC.description:
Represent and analyze quantitative relationships by:
  • Using variables to represent two quantities in a real-world or mathematical context that change in relationship to one another.
  • Analyze the relationship between quantities in different representations (context, equations, tables, and graphs).

036E1946002D4576B443C01793D0DA6F.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

E28851D972DA42B1B6354E646477DB39.description:
Reason about inequalities by:
  • Using substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an inequality true.
  • Writing an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem.
  • Recognizing that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions.
  • Representing solutions of inequalities on number line diagrams.

5D159E5A36004AB98DD9DC1717CBC4A6.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form:
  • x + p = q in which p, q and x are all non-negative rational numbers; and,
  • p · x = q for cases in which p, q and x are all non-negative rational numbers.

28106A39FAC64FCBBAF9DF9582298FAF.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem.

84E7A10618C046CA8DB10D17D8CA9E66.description: Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation true.

389300DD0B714CCDA360F1B8F48FB945.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations.

098E75FAC7AC44E9ACBC7B6A054CCE19.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent and justify with mathematical reasoning.

410EE0010C494B0DADBC8353A9B1991A.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions without exponents.

FFD48C72E3B847AEBF6CAD4DCF4DD0B3.description:
Write, read, and evaluate algebraic expressions.
  • Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.
  • Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms and view one or more of those parts as a single entity.
  • Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables using expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems.

F7B2FDF24B7D4C0AA4CCEDA75D3CB9FE.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions, with and without grouping symbols, involving whole-number exponents.

A527F6766CD54E1F8A101144798AB00E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

9EA67C2D263B4237BC1DB1D017F29A38.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction.Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.Understand p + q as the number located a distance q from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on the sign of q. Show that a number and its additive inverse create a zero pair.Understand subtraction of integers as adding the additive inverse, p - q = p + (-q). Show that the distance between two integers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference.Use models to add and subtract integers from -20 to 20 and describe real-world contexts using sums and differences.

1190920757AB4E9587913FC5660D0511.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

4BF8DD0EB4CE473981E2DB356021A07B.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

50849906E35545A491547F5150127FEC.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.

86F412A4389F408F84443B1E92FDEB9C.description:
On a coordinate plane:
  • Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants.
  • Recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.
  • Find and position pairs of rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

B341F5E3B0E34C0CA5538D6832B20B51.description:
On a number line:
  • Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 and that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself.
  • Find and position rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line.

FB5101408A5E47FBBF0830D374E38808.description: Understand rational numbers as points on the number line and as ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

06A34BBA746F4DCB9D01F3E1CBB21B35.description:
Understand and use rational numbers to:
  • Describe quantities having opposite directions or values.
  • Represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.
  • Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line to:
    • Interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world context.
    • Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

8D6BEDE969694D9DAECB427FE974A377.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

B616E214B921407E87ED8D12C608D58B.description:
Understand and use prime factorization and the relationships between factors to:
  • Find the unique prime factorization for a whole number.
  • Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100.
  • Use the greatest common factor and the distributive property to rewrite the sum of two whole numbers, each less than or equal to 100.
  • Find the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12 to add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators.

023D0AFF866B48A380A9DEDAA883EA55.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of decimals to develop and fluently use the standard algorithms for addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of decimals.

C2971F246C1A4EF4A17390062745D638.description: Fluently divide using long division with a minimum of a four-digit dividend and interpret the quotient and remainder in context.

B47AD5564DAA460AA04A5A57292E6876.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

434FEEAE83454A2381D35C8A3FEC8F70.description:
Use visual models and common denominators to:
  • Interpret and compute quotients of fractions.
  • Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving division of fractions.

65616F07CC9B4A29A45955ADFA88591B.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

15DE58D02E5C4EB7BF009486A90B5A65.description:
Use ratio reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems with percents by:
  • Understanding and finding a percent of a quantity as a ratio per 100.
  • Using equivalent ratios, such as benchmark percents (50%, 25%, 10%, 5%, 1%), to determine a part of any given quantity.
  • Finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

E4D31D51720B42C3B2B385AD13831AE0.description:
Use ratio reasoning with equivalent whole-number ratios to solve real-world and mathematical problems by:
  • Creating and using a table to compare ratios.
  • Finding missing values in the tables.
  • Using a unit ratio.
  • Converting and manipulating measurements using given ratios.
  • Plotting the pairs of values on the coordinate plane.

E37A292EF25548CAAB748D669888F72F.description: Understand that ratios can be expressed as equivalent unit ratios by finding and interpreting both unit ratios in context.

A1740B7643984C7CBF32C7E4A0BDE49B.description:
Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to:
  • Describe a ratio as a multiplicative relationship between two quantities.
  • Model a ratio relationship using a variety of representations.

47A64E616CB44FEBB5703C8438D55A0F.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

B7773C0ECA014C2592A45363A37D1C63.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

138F52E7D9774DAAAD0CD22FE795335F.description: Look for and make use of structure.

9193A467F83440B1AA19F517B3A92947.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

FC6CF23BDB754B8B8BC8A69BA6B1E2AB.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Carolina Standard Course of Study K-8 Mathematics

A077659920474F0C819DDFA7194305CF.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

6131F9A48C3A4117B5E43EC6FF8EA3D7.description: For an event described in everyday language, identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event, when the sample space is represented using organized lists, tables, and tree diagrams.

9CE967CB0F574CD094E04BC7BC689090.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

2101835D95D04D1CBCE3FCDFF50E6B22.description: Determine probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

AA727DC6892F44CCAB22AD27B1523793.description: Compare theoretical and experimental probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

495951FD160844128F11A9E6557AB99E.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by repeatedly performing a chance process and observing frequencies in the data generated.

8E327D249BB44F1685A7B848C12DB5B3.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

14409E41E72C407D8146E743CF03542A.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of simple events.

F89DBB51E3554C4E9B27CE86DA3BA538.description: Collect data to calculate the experimental probability of a chance event, observing its long-run relative frequency. Use this experimental probability to predict the approximate relative frequency.

D95E7EC8C4A248C68377D3B5B35B032C.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring.

93B3D9BDC1E74A08BFE51DB216F3BFE0.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

31BBDA8DCB184B17936400C852599D71.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw comparative inferences about two populations.

0C3D2E0052554A059C64D213E53BA06C.description: Informally assess the difference between two data sets by examining the overlap and separation between the graphical representations of two data sets.

6FB8D47C37DE4EBD9034CD769D026AB8.description:
Calculate the measure of variability of a data set and understand that it describes how the values of the data set vary with a single number.
  • Understand the mean absolute deviation of a data set is a measure of variability that describes the average distance that points within a data set are from the mean of the data set.
  • Understand that the range describes the spread of the entire data set.
  • Understand that the interquartile range describes the spread of the middle 50% of the data.

6619F76E6BFD49CB94A0DAD24F23DA47.description: Recognize the role of variability when comparing two populations.

18499C010BF640F18850C2F3B8AC6633.description: Make informal inferences to compare two populations.

0EBD8C881D224AC68EF097C5A3CAA288.description: Generate multiple random samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions, and use this data to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest.

8AAF7E4F5AC645EA86E1C9A615481C3A.description:
Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by:
  • Recognizing that generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population.
  • Using random sampling to produce representative samples to support valid inferences.

984FE7803F724301A4E2E18B6B7FC0D4.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

9245D283A2BF45AB9D19293C0241407B.description:
Construct inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
  • Fluently solve multi-step inequalities with the variable on one side, including those generated by word problems.
  • Compare an algebraic solution process for equations and an algebraic solution process for inequalities.
  • Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret in context.

C05F30D59425478C8CFF1740E3305FF9.description:
Construct equations to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
  • Fluently solve multistep equations with the variable on one side, including those generated by word problems.
  • Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.
  • Interpret the solution in context.

4754FB7AC1464EB5B7798048BA1296FC.description: Use variables to represent quantities to solve real-world or mathematical problems.

79EFC37F74234EDCA0929A90F2BB9F5E.description:
Solve multi-step real-world and mathematical problems posed with rational numbers in algebraic expressions.
  • Apply properties of operations to calculate with positive and negative numbers in any form.
  • Convert between different forms of a number and equivalent forms of the expression as appropriate.

FB1CA7268A2E47429760CA72124938C4.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions, equations, and inequalities.

E9DC583505324F419E0CD3F345DFB8EB.description: Understand that equivalent expressions can reveal real-world and mathematical relationships. Interpret the meaning of the parts of each expression in context.

000DE85F55164BE4AA552E80D299E067.description:
Apply properties of operations as strategies to:
  • Add, subtract, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
  • Factor linear expression with an integer GCF.

7B494F6625D54A12A3A9537410C040ED.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

B65BB228C5A547BF90E704976183EE03.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving numerical expressions with rational numbers using the four operations.

C27905E2060C4D8C84F04A047FE9FF63.description:
Use division and previous understandings of fractions and decimals.
  • Convert a fraction to a decimal using long division.
  • Understand that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

7E7D7D058FB84628AC975375ED7B4481.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies, including the standard algorithms, to multiply and divide rational numbers and describe the product and quotient in real-world contexts.

5F5F5080A7D84B8C89DADA0D8AF37A5A.description: Understand that a rational number is any number that can be written as a quotient of integers with a non-zero divisor.

2D77B47A11164688904F6D20DCB03105.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division.

51E5F26DF8F9482DB6BA739741AA033D.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers, using the properties of operations, and describing real-world contexts using sums and differences.

4BD62E11B5EA4B2C8643FF4A0B33D4D0.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

DFBFDC828EFB403CBB213A0A09276CF1.description: Use scale factors and unit rates in proportional relationships to solve ratio and percent problems.

CB545F035A334BE1AEB7CC4AC48692E5.description:
Use a graphical representation of a proportional relationship in context to:
  • Explain the meaning of any point (x, y).
  • Explain the meaning of (0, 0) and why it is included.
  • Understand that the y-coordinate of the ordered pair (1, r) corresponds to the unit rate and explain its meaning.

3E4DC829F95C413485D729498AA227D2.description: Create equations and graphs to represent proportional relationships.

16CEEFBBDB1149E8AEECB4E89F147430.description: Identify the unit rate (constant of proportionality) within two quantities in a proportional relationship using tables, graphs, equations, and verbal descriptions.

67B88F3ABF26409D91FD0A2EE2D606E9.description:
Understand that a proportion is a relationship of equality between ratios.
  • Represent proportional relationships using tables and graphs.
  • Recognize whether ratios are in a proportional relationship using tables and graphs.
  • Compare two different proportional relationships using tables, graphs, equations, and verbal descriptions.

FEAE0D1FFFB346B49623DFC4E77C5269.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

84FF5C8E043D4F95A0750E7235ED438C.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

28EB1E3B774748059979CD55A63818C9.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

553F429C0CAF44E284C66B455D8F94B1.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving:
  • Area and perimeter of two-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons.
  • Volume and surface area of pyramids, prisms, or three-dimensional objects composed of cubes, pyramids, and right prisms.

BF14EBDBD6624E708C7AB3DC10F8E730.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

9D2AA69BC98A47C4B16D6F9523D580E7.description:
Understand area and circumference of a circle.
  • Understand the relationships between the radius, diameter, circumference, and area.
  • Apply the formulas for area and circumference of a circle to solve problems.

5A968CB91D474C6FB4B42FAB34B4CA3E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

94661914A3C040BF811BC46DCBD73B04.description: Understand the characteristics of angles and side lengths that create a unique triangle, more than one triangle or no triangle. Build triangles from three measures of angles and/or sides.

002011DD353C447A8760394A00B4D9D1.description:
Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures by:
  • Building an understanding that angle measures remain the same and side lengths are proportional.
  • Using a scale factor to compute actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing.
  • Creating a scale drawing.

F5CCD07D47494D1692A5DE954F5E4F21.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

C94DB61973C145A9A61692506B4C71D4.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

55623FA8CC234702AB351F214F068DE5.description: Look for and make use of structure.

206AB2A9351C4A5BBF4B94B2C5786D60.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

BE23B25A6A9041DE8B59BBE3AD0C9FE3.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Carolina Standard Course of Study K-8 Mathematics

C138691D3742418D827221BAABBEE9B8.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size using area and length models, and recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole.

855910CA3AB94642913190C14189C138.description:
Use decimal notation to represent fractions.
  • Express, model and explain the equivalence between fractions with denominators of 10 and 100.
  • Use equivalent fractions to add two fractions with denominators of 10 or 100.
  • Represent tenths and hundredths with models, making connections between fractions and decimals.

017629D238A64CC8867486E83F8308AB.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

D4E6BC0408D8496A80D6ACFCC083FD04.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to:
  • Model and explain how fractions can be represented by multiplying a whole number by a unit fraction, using this understanding to multiply a whole number by any fraction less than one.
  • Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number.

5FECEB2C030D42468CB764B8143CA813.description: Use unit fractions to understand operations of fractions.

57FD82C54D784C77B1B68DBCE9C332FA.description:
Understand and justify decompositions of fractions with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.
  • Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
  • Decompose a fraction into a sum of unit fractions and a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way using area models, length models, and equations.
  • Add and subtract fractions, including mixed numbers with like denominators, by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
  • Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions, including mixed numbers by writing equations from a visual representation of the problem.

66B3BDA1EB614667A7C020D1CDAC8E2F.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

6BE538962E22451AAA3567E85733E6AB.description:
Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, using the denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions by:
  • Reasoning about their size and using area and length models.
  • Using benchmark fractions 0, ½, and a whole.
  • Comparing common numerator or common denominators.

A21BA6B098BD499988466D06313C1FB5.description: Explain why a fraction is equivalent to another fraction by using area and length fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size.

F8BC0CCBAC224ED29B08651A6BA73DD7.description: Recognize symmetry in a two-dimensional figure, and identify and draw lines of symmetry.

54664A96CCE24991A328FC4A78E2D9C3.description: Classify quadrilaterals and triangles based on angle measure, side lengths, and the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines.

4AAF2FD67CF945CABA6B47FD38BDAEC2.description: Draw and identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles, and perpendicular and parallel lines.

98A930B699A24EDDAEBCD44A4691EE1E.description: Classify shapes based on lines and angles in two-dimensional figures.

6C307DC52609474C810B86042EC8145F.description:
Develop an understanding of angles and angle measurement.
  • Understand angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and are measured in degrees.
  • Measure and sketch angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor.
  • Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems.

848F39BDE8344D22AEDD9FE6E7D11A47.description: Understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

9F957D66A0B44EEB9D7E0520063FE2D2.description:
Solve problems with area and perimeter.
  • Find areas of rectilinear figures with known side lengths.
  • Solve problems involving a fixed area and varying perimeters and a fixed perimeter and varying areas.
  • Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.

53301E0268A945218D19D496C0A05021.description: Solve problems involving area and perimeter.

E379BAFD2FEE42CD94D56B43FAD5E98F.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals that cross the hour.

3B378B4ADE9A4208924A10D0AA6AEFDC.description: Use multiplicative reasoning to convert metric measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit using place value understanding, two-column tables, and length models.

5CA3F2C68E8D450CA8C9FE2748C6BA87.description:
Know relative sizes of measurement units. Solve problems involving metric measurement.
  • Measure to solve problems involving metric units: centimeter, meter, gram, kilogram, Liter, milliliter.
  • Add, subtract, multiply, and divide to solve one-step word problems involving whole-number measurements of length, mass, and capacity that are given in metric units.

0F2212C3D5DB488E8D61CB4536674E4E.description:
Represent and interpret data using whole numbers.
  • Collect data by asking a question that yields numerical data.
  • Make a representation of data and interpret data in a frequency table, scaled bar graph, and/or line plot.
  • Determine whether a survey question will yield categorical or numerical data.

5A2165B8225E4A2496A7EC2EA4ABC30B.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to three-digit dividends and one-digit divisors with place value understanding using rectangular arrays, area models, repeated subtraction, partial quotients, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division.

8BED5F61E4CA49D49FF39E3D4A71F9F5.description: Multiply a whole number of up to three digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply up to two two-digit numbers with place value understanding using area models, partial products, and the properties of operations. Use models to make connections and develop the algorithm.

6EB89307B0A0431794C14EBC066FA81A.description: Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers up to and including 100,000 using the standard algorithm with place value understanding.

7CC979200FE44DEF8AA5638CFF4FDB49.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

7C373E8CD6E24D6FA8B152803D7BB143.description: Compare two multi-digit numbers up to and including 100,000 based on the values of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

87EC5B309687417AAB009EA33FBB3385.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers up to and including 100,000 using numerals, number names, and expanded form.

770A34AC0ED94666B429558C75717619.description: Explain that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right, up to 100,000.

324458FADACE49C5A168DD4510E2CEDC.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit numbers whole numbers.

3458750C8EB249B8BD7ECB4B76BBEB35.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

E08AF529551343CEA50D3197018D5B30.description: Generate and analyze a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule.

154F18090C0548818A72C56E2F51162A.description:
Find all factor pairs for whole numbers up to and including 50 to:
  • Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors.
  • Determine whether a given whole number is a multiple of a given one-digit number.
  • Determine if the number is prime or composite.

30B8C87351C94D1AB571178AB1C4FED5.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

C8C17F4C2AC84BA09B9F3809BD0B107E.description:
Solve two-step word problems involving the four operations with whole numbers.
  • Use estimation strategies to assess reasonableness of answers.
  • Interpret remainders in word problems.
  • Represent problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.

39494B983E2D4239AE6E1CEF08BDB40D.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

A7CB78C657764341965C7FECFBD958D1.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

7B287DA87B5645BEB1F90165314144EE.description: Look for and make use of structure.

3C78592F18434AC28F6137ADFFAE89DC.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

6A4353783E9641019B6F41525746835B.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Carolina Standard Course of Study K-8 Mathematics

F953CEA3AE1F4A2C8B0A8F4FE5627471.description:
Reason with two-dimensional shapes and their attributes.
• Investigate, describe, and reason about composing triangles and quadrilaterals and decomposing quadrilaterals.
• Recognize and draw examples and non-examples of types of quadrilaterals including rhombuses, rectangles, squares, parallelograms,
and trapezoids.

372BA012F1834D65A4340A25C81E62DF.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

60EF0872C9C146B5929FE7BDEBE99972.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size, using area and length models, and using the >, <, and = symbols. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole with denominators: halves, fourths and eighths; thirds and sixths.

87CF05056F02490D9F4D92531A93C452.description:
Represent equivalent fractions with area and length models by:
  • Composing and decomposing fractions into equivalent fractions using related fractions: halves, fourths and eighths; thirds and sixths.
  • Explaining that a fraction with the same numerator and denominator equals one whole.
  • Expressing whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

652CC2AAF04742FB9655BC86368A1669.description:
Interpret fractions with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 using area and length models.
  • Using an area model, explain that the numerator of a fraction represents the number of equal parts of the unit fraction.
  • Using a number line, explain that the numerator of a fraction represents the number of lengths of the unit fraction from 0.

4EC6B1EB1D864C13B39CAA4B116CE67F.description:
Interpret unit fractions with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 as quantities formed when a whole is partitioned into equal parts;
  • Explain that a unit fraction is one of those parts.
  • Represent and identify unit fractions using area and length models.

4C461754373349D2972E88B9597A3431.description: Solve problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, and finding an unknown side length.

FCA047B8B20E4918A81AF9679FC96F74.description:
Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.
  • Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
  • Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.
  • Use tiles and/or arrays to illustrate and explain that the area of a rectangle can be found by partitioning it into two smaller rectangles, and that the area of the large rectangle is the sum of the two smaller rectangles.

B6A12F2FAB724D45B07C9AFB339DE038.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling without gaps or overlaps and counting unit squares.

F2DED63F93764EE8ADAE137ACA2ABC0C.description:
Solve problems involving customary measurement.
  • Estimate and measure lengths in customary units to the quarter-inch and half-inch, and feet and yards to the whole unit.
  • Estimate and measure capacity and weight in customary units to a whole number: cups, pints, quarts, gallons, ounces, and pounds.
  • Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving whole number measurements of length, weight, and capacity in the same customary units.

2A215DE9B67C454892D05C024EAFAE0B.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals within the same hour.

3D195ECE09EA4C8980B87838D53F580B.description:
Represent and interpret scaled picture and bar graphs:
  • Collect data by asking a question that yields data in up to four categories.
  • Make a representation of data and interpret data in a frequency table, scaled picture graph, and/or scaled bar graph with axes provided.
  • Solve one and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information from these graphs.

7F1CAED7B1B74901A48E45B5DC108E57.description: Use concrete and pictorial models, based on place value and the properties of operations, to find the product of a one-digit whole number by a multiple of 10 in the range 10–90.

7E6257C078BA411CBD04D4AAEC338B42.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit numbers.

814F7FA4A3E9481B868260EF72CF2685.description:
Add and subtract whole numbers up to and including 1,000.
  • Use estimation strategies to assess reasonableness of answers.
  • Model and explain how the relationship between addition and subtraction can be applied to solve addition and subtraction problems.
  • Use expanded form to decompose numbers and then find sums and differences.

77C10CB9B70E4CA4941DCCBCC10EEF9A.description: Use place value to add and subtract.

9CB03595F08D4C20BF490CA9C99D7FF1.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

4ACBCB62B70744CD9FEB4017AAE0675F.description: Interpret patterns of multiplication on a hundreds board and/or multiplication table.

B5977B22373148AEBAFFD79B10DD383A.description: Solve two-step word problems using addition, subtraction, and multiplication, representing problems using equations with a symbol for the unknown number.

D01D6B992C8A4EA5A0FA426BF73EEF1A.description:
Demonstrate fluency with multiplication and division with factors, quotients and divisors up to and including 10.
  • Know from memory all products with factors up to and including 10.
  • Illustrate and explain using the relationship between multiplication and division.
  • Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.

C907073675F64712B84266806539CB71.description: Solve an unknown-factor problem, by using division strategies and/or changing it to a multiplication problem.

405B53BBB19043F7B3869C00372D95C9.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

DF004DCF0B9F4C2DBF4C13CBCA7FE4D0.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison. Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparisons using models and equations with a symbol for the unknown number. Distinguish multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

5EDDA57B6D8E44C5954FCDC412843289.description:
Represent, interpret, and solve one-step problems involving multiplication and division.
  • Solve multiplication word problems with factors up to and including 10. Represent the problem using arrays, pictures, and/or equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
  • Solve division word problems with a divisor and quotient up to and including 10. Represent the problem using arrays, pictures, repeated subtraction and/or equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

37C2355638A14A20B38BF787F8B66C1F.description:
For whole-number quotients of whole numbers with a one-digit divisor and a one-digit quotient:
  • Interpret the divisor and quotient in a division equation as representing the number of equal groups and the number of objects in each group.
  • Illustrate and explain strategies including arrays, repeated addition or subtraction, and decomposing a factor.

83E62FCB1A464EE4A18C818DD40153BF.description:
For products of whole numbers with two factors up to and including 10:
  • Interpret the factors as representing the number of equal groups and the number of objects in each group.
  • Illustrate and explain strategies including arrays, repeated addition, decomposing a factor, and applying the commutative and associative properties.

DE6680EF743446839E5E8F4BFB030D71.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

68F7A983DE3E4498B0BCC6E57447B472.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

701BFAAFC4634197982C507E1200A5B0.description: Look for and make use of structure.

297FD70B350B4B76B12673A4BACC3171.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

67785538695D455BB8F57FA100E1BF64.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Carolina Standard Course of Study for English Language Arts

6BC524CD656E44188BF742497DBCBD34.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; develop vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

1D54DCE039624EDAA352A39AA35C8FCF.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in developing vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

1A1064B72E0A40A6BAFCF7633BD81E7F.description: Distinguish among the connotations of words with similar denotations.

78AC1A86B14C482B93F3FD4A9CD4224E.description: Interpret figures of speech in context based on grade 7 reading and content.

A5F1F41E7F934BB7A65D4889083EDD59.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language and nuances in word meanings.

32CCF79F183444A0B2F210847378D6A2.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language and nuances in word meanings.

48663BCAB67042F0904835ACFCCA8E15.description: Determine and/or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 7 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies: context clues, word parts, word relationships, and reference materials.

EBFB9D9669034D668A463B0527A99A68.description: Determine and/or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, word relationships, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

39CE6C4436F243E48658E118B0E08F2A.description: Choose language that expresses ideas precisely and concisely, recognizing and eliminating wordiness and redundancy.

FDE904DE7F3540FF98F942D540F87A85.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

538FDC3C73BD47649704CD45B38852B0.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

953D6BD432544939AF29EAE5E6BF6582.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing; demonstrate proficiency within the 6-8 conventions continuum.

76E2918A50314E6DB65FCCDD8F327732.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing; demonstrate proficiency within the appropriate grade band conventions continuum.

BAE9EE3C650348B1A1AA852FF26CD23D.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; demonstrate proficiency within the 6-8 grammar continuum.

FBCBEF06E3C246728013B1B906657DC5.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; demonstrate proficiency within the appropriate grade band grammar continuum.

7A9723FEC6AE459BB614A587369EF60D.description: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify claims and findings and emphasize salient points.

167C44BF3E8B437BBDC63F3A573AD381.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

E745F5025A564DF4BAB123753785B31A.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with pertinent descriptions, facts, details, and examples; adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks.

B06BF5C289D24D22A608950BDA26991F.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

239F006F77294C2DBC24E6C48B70AF18.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

54BC0F6529ED43C5B72A6AD53589364A.description:
Leaders will advocate for positive change in the community and encourage 
       others to pursue community service.

ED373456DAC343599DBD538C0130D7BE.description:
Leaders will demonstrate and devise ways to assume active consistent roles 
       in their communities.

7CA2574DECB546DCAB6C8BB73C3F522D.description:
Leaders will demonstrate and present ways that they and others can be 
involved in their communities.

D1E4200B272E461CAAAAE70B34026831.description:
Leaders demonstrate that citizenship requires gathering information, 
       Making informed choices and acting responsibly.

AAE975DBEACE4ADEA9410FCBB6956CA1.description:
Leaders will evaluate the needs of communities within the school, city, 	
      county, state, nation, and world.

681872D8463C477B8F529A1F9381ECB3.description: Leaders identify needs within their community and seek to create change.

608C2D858696464FAC443A28171F784E.description:

                                  conversation.

56A921BB65B7418DABD6169F8804E89C.description: Leaders will facilitate the mediation of simulated conflicts.

D544B45B43E34F0A9D20B1A1AEDB389C.description: Leaders will analyze conflicts and evaluate conflict resolution skills.

Leaders will recognize the necessity of compromise in various leadership 
		       situations.

EEA2500FCBBE45808089BADD3A045493.description:
Leaders engage in open, safe and direct dialogue to advance learning and 
	resolve potential conflicts.

4925039AEDC644D1B69DB7BA07199A87.description: Leaders will effectively articulate their personal agenda to the community.

7161BB5EE4104079A34832D14FEAD2F3.description:
Leaders will present their personal vision to a group in persuasive
                                  but not domineering ways.

0188D035387247AC91D3D87FC76ABB9A.description: Leaders will recognize the value of people over tasks.

E8724D4C153E435087E6F9BFE38DFEE7.description: Leaders will identify the communities in which they are involved.

5CC03E64C87345D69C6C481A5DE259AC.description:

	healthy community.

6AAC3BD497D44BB789100A35AFDD0E57.description: Leaders will identify and value consensus in heterogeneous groups.

9025D2F2B5BD46FDB6FCEED3D78A0384.description:
Leaders will communicate effectively in pairs, teams, small and large
		       groups.

9367EC71C23D49BB80C8A7BA3E623205.description: Leaders will balance personal expression with others’ contributions.

13B5A0F5595C4DD19C8FF3CFF411F67A.description: Leaders will practice active listening skills.

A9D0BE40B9934ECDAC7B96CFA579C470.description: Leaders will distinguish fact from opinion.

AA929B034C3846C9A0BEDD1532302629.description:
Leaders will identify and value differing perspectives and their influence              
 		upon leadership, such as gender, ethnicity, political affiliation, religion and socio-                    
economics.

D4CF1E24D71C4315863E2697B6A84B5E.description:
Leaders allow others to provide ideas from various perspectives and 
	participate in decisions.

F6886AB6961E4677A619B84749629D9C.description: Leaders will define and demonstrate academic integrity.

F39215F159CE42F9A1A698220EC4C485.description: Leaders will investigate the consequences of a lack of character and integrity.

76A1AFA63A474687B6B96130AC6E7AEA.description:
Leaders will explore philosophical concepts associated with leadership such
		       as virtue and justice.

7C77270E29E34E2AA8712C7CC784B34D.description: Leaders will compare and contrast leadership theories and styles.

BFF135C4483C453D9CECA0986C75A01B.description: Leaders will identify key character qualities and principles of leaders.

F94BB4E740C04B67BD1D9B7FE3F45CA9.description: Leaders develop leadership identity by exhibiting character and integrity.

B431C45F8B2548B6A51122B50FD2D3E2.description:
Leaders will revise goals and expectations as they evaluate their progress 
       academically and socially.

E8F229BE8E3F4CF1920CB8C48EAD549D.description:
Leaders will outline an internal conflict resolution practice and demonstrate        
       this through scenarios and reflections.

C55BB5399EC642359B5508F8F263244A.description: Leaders will reflect upon past failures and identify associated growth.

639D1E5509C44CC0A508277B82CE1056.description: Leaders will evaluate leaders based upon their persistence in struggles.

474527D7967B4FC382087D916555281A.description: Leaders will define and demonstrate resilience and grit.

4C85014A6BAC4AA1860B7BB3E586162D.description:
Leaders demonstrate persistence in the face of challenges, accept 
             responsibility and grow through failure.

D0A19677F72B4F7F8BA61B2A8EB2422B.description: Leaders will design and participate in leadership projects and events.

11C6BF5C766C4176B8492F236B90FA5E.description: Leaders will justify the need for diverse leaders and followers.

A174811C1B3645BAA146DA8CBBF48EBA.description:
Leaders will analyze the complex, evolving relationships between leaders and 
	                    those they lead.

7112936557EE4F92A17FC8E1974B4D4E.description: Leaders will define and recognize the need for leadership multiplication.

E9C00BCB7AE84556A4E045BCE36131EA.description:
Leaders build leaders who build leaders. Leaders develop and empower 
             others.

017B2F33204948E3B0C7F4ECC6295D13.description:
Leaders will execute goals for themselves academically, socially
		       and physically.

C9E0719BF9AE463B880CCC0C0C2B5798.description:
Leaders will reflect on and  describe ways that they have developed 
       academically, socially, and physically in the past and present.

E973A4DBD2E94706886798508C19581E.description:
Leaders will evaluate their own behaviors and identify the consequences for
		       both them and others.

80705A55C222438ABAB7236F6C62F607.description:
Leaders will evaluate their own self-image including their interests, values, 
		      skills, strengths, weaknesses, and styles.

A4BBA95F3451403EBDA8106B5F769398.description:
Leaders seek, throughout their life, to grow in academics, social skills, and 
	physical and emotional health.

81556159763E4DD9A7E0AB1D502D4B11.description:
Leaders will define commitment and what it means to apply it to different     
                    areas of life.

A11647F09D5E424F93C0A56629E76A69.description: Leaders will conduct student-led academic conferences.

1D91288865224BC1A19DE16B9B694BCE.description: Leaders will design academic and leadership plans for themselves.

789E5CB6610A41AB9FF722867E3CED6D.description:
Leaders will discuss goal setting and formulate goals for 
      themselves.
