244E46A648024F85A337FAEFFFB90D4F.description: Leaders will analyze leaders and identify traits they want to emulate.

6C98976AA9CE4611836E0CE460AC291C.description: Leaders will discuss what leadership is and what leadership is not.

1543D35BFAC64AB6B63BC0040C975130.description: Leaders set clear direction, align to it, and commit to success.

document.title: North Carolina State Board of Education

D1FD6ED52683480F870A5BC68D3584A7.description:
Analyze multiple perceptions of the “American Dream” in times of prosperity and crisis
since Reconstruction (e.g., Great Depression, Dust Bowl, New Deal, oil crisis, savings and
loan crisis, dot.com bubble, mortgage foreclosure crisis, etc.).

3C12EBDE6CD243BA9B655C254786A6F0.description:
Evaluate the extent to which a variety of groups and individuals have had opportunity to
attain their perception of the “American Dream” since Reconstruction (e.g., immigrants,
Flappers, Rosie the Riveter, GIs, blue collar worker, white collar worker, etc.).

709750F66BA242BAB2545FC55A1AD3A0.description:
Explain how opportunity and mobility impacted various groups within American society
since Reconstruction (e.g., Americanization movement, settlement house movement, Dust
Bowl, the Great Migration, suburbia, etc.).

33194B464DA249DAAA1A38FA6702F5FA.description:
Analyze the relationship between innovation, economic development, progress and various
perceptions of the “American Dream” since Reconstruction (e.g., Gilded Age, assembly
line, transcontinental railroad, highway system, credit, etc.).

320A9ED9EF2C4F0D9E48680C2CBB5CFD.description:
Essential Standard: Analyze the
relationship between
progress, crisis and
the “American
Dream” within the
United States.

AE74D1D800BB4CCBA9F4856ACBCC1834.description:
Explain the impact of wars on American society and culture since Reconstruction (e.g.,
relocation of Japanese Americans, American propaganda, first and second Red Scare
movement, McCarthyism, baby boom, Civil Rights Movement, protest movements, ethnic,
patriotism, etc.).

16C15A5C59A94CFD97F6126F1C007B71.description:
Explain the impact of wars on the American economy since Reconstruction (e.g.,
mobilizing for war, war industries, rationing, women in the workforce, lend-lease policy,
WWII farming gains, GI Bill, etc.).

7683598D5F56478E9948E1E4308C0242.description:
Explain the impact of wars on American politics since Reconstruction (e.g., spheres of
influence, isolationist practices, containment policies, first and second Red Scare
movements, patriotism, terrorist policies, etc.).

F58CA7E3AAFA470CB03A4C8C9E9A3935.description:
Essential Standard: Understand the
impact of war on
American politics,
economics, society
and culture.

2930B489D96F4701B21334A040FEFED4.description:
Explain the reasons for United States involvement in global wars and the influence each
involvement had on international affairs (e.g., Spanish-American War, WWI, WWII, Cold
War, Korea, Vietnam, Gulf War, Iraqi War, etc.).

E235402C430C48DF8F6EA52FAA79F408.description:
Explain how national economic and political interests helped set the direction of United
States foreign policy since Reconstruction (e.g., new markets, isolationism, neutrality,
containment, homeland security, etc.).

05AC0D25085540A4A3A8C972C3D91C52.description:
Essential Standards: Understand how and
why the role of the
United States in the
world has changed
over time.

CF0B82C88CA04B879B18E4FF1A9E27A2.description:
Explain how judicial, legislative and executive actions have affected the distribution of
power between levels of government since Reconstruction (e.g., New Deal, Great Society,
Civil Rights, etc.).

7D6A41D4DC174A4691F7528A3FDFEE97.description:
Summarize how the philosophical, ideological and/or religious views on freedom and
equality contributed to the development of American political and economic systems since
Reconstruction (e.g., “separate but equal”, Social Darwinism, social gospel, civil service
system, suffrage, Harlem Renaissance, the Warren Court, Great Society programs,
American Indian Movement, etc.).

E1ACFEEF24A64158981FB0FFED2F8F21.description:
Essential Standard: Understand how
tensions between
freedom, equality and
power have shaped
the political, economic
and social
development of the
United States.

4A720E6727DB42BC80AD0C85A14092DF.description:
Analyze the cultural conflicts that impacted the United States since Reconstruction and the
compromises that resulted (e.g., nativism, Back to Africa movement, modernism,
fundamentalism, black power movement, women’s movement, counterculture, Wilmington
Race Riots, etc.).

DF0E8F48CEF441ADA765D4870B6E49DB.description:
Analyze the social and religious conflicts, movements and reforms that impacted the United
States since Reconstruction in terms of participants, strategies, opposition, and results (e.g.,
Prohibition, Social Darwinism, Eugenics, civil rights, anti-war protest, etc.).
AH2.H.4.4 Analyze the cultural conflicts that impacted the United States since Reconstruction and

4E516EDC6C504644A06E16752AC137DC.description:
Analyze the economic issues and conflicts that impacted the United States since
Reconstruction and the compromises that resulted (e.g., currency policy, industrialization,
urbanization, laissez-faire, labor unrest, New Deal, Great Society, supply-side economics,
etc.).

170348DC353E449DB45E5403B5199247.description:
Analyze the political issues and conflicts that impacted the United States since
Reconstruction and the compromises that resulted (e.g., Populism, Progressivism, working
conditions and labor unrest, New Deal, Wilmington Race Riots, Eugenics, Civil Rights
Movement, Anti-War protests, Watergate, etc.).

96F51331C51D412187930FCB89715A54.description:
Essential Standard: Analyze how conflict
and compromise have
shaped politics,
economics and culture
in the United States.

666481899FEB41BA96AA9D3CF42F2FFF.description:
Analyze voluntary and involuntary immigration trends since Reconstruction in terms of
causes, regions of origin and destination, cultural contributions, and public and
governmental response (e.g., new immigrants, ports of entry, ethnic neighborhoods,
settlement houses, immigration restrictions, etc.).

A9BE88617C2E4A139B89C0104AF43F89.description:
Explain the roles of various racial and ethnic groups in settlement and expansion since
Reconstruction and the consequences for those groups (e.g., American Indians, African
Americans, Chinese, Irish, Hispanics and Latino Americans, Asian Americans, etc.).

076E5872F4864EC48468F1ADCE6DB794.description:
Explain how environmental, cultural and economic factors influenced the patterns of
migration and settlement within the United States since the end of Reconstruction (e.g.,
gold rush, destruction of the buffalo, reservations, ethnic neighborhoods, etc.).

66A486FA3F334577ADBC583AC97B52C3.description:
Analyze how economic, political, social, military and religious factors influenced United
States imperialism (e.g., passing of the western frontier, new markets, Spanish American
War, Open Door Policy, Monroe Doctrine, Roosevelt Corollary, canal routes, etc.).

DA1891EF16C24F1591827D10AA31ABA3.description:
Essential Standard: Understand the
factors that led to
exploration,
settlement, movement,
and expansion and
their impact on
United States
development over
time.

98AB7BAB0EBC487A86E6ED89A3E9146C.description:
Evaluate key turning points since the end of Reconstruction in terms of their lasting impact
(e.g., conflicts, legislation, elections, innovations, leadership, movements, Supreme Court
decisions, etc.).

26A8B03CA06C412EB49A9628DD670357.description:
Analyze key political, economic, and social turning points since the end of Reconstruction
in terms of causes and effects (e.g., conflicts, legislation, elections, innovations, leadership,
movements, Supreme Court decisions, etc.).

79780300BBA54997895DB89560340900.description:
Essential Standard: Analyze key political,
economic and social
turning points in
American History
using historical
thinking.

AED79F5E41144822962193F997F64CCC.description:
Use Historical Research to:1. Formulate historical questions.
2. Obtain historical data from a variety of sources.
3. Support interpretations with historical evidence.
4. Construct analytical essays using historical evidence to support arguments.

492C6F8A391A4D2EA1C44FBF4EDC8EA0.description:
Use Historical Analysis and Interpretation to:1. Identify issues and problems of the past.
2. Consider multiple perspectives of various peoples of the past.
3. Analyze cause-and-effect relationships and multiple causation.
4. Evaluate competing historical narratives and debates among historians.
5. Evaluate the influence of the past on contemporary issues.

2219DEE7A92A4090B5B11E4E93E04B3A.description:
Use Historical Comprehension to:1. Reconstruct the literal meaning of a historical passage.
2. Differentiate between historical facts and historical interpretations.
3. Analyze data in historical maps.
4. Analyze visual, literary and musical sources.

9E1B438DE93641F1B67F10CAE86E06C9.description:
Analyze multiple perceptions of the “American
Dream” in times of prosperity and crisis
through Reconstruction (e.g., Hamilton’s
Financial Plan; Embargo of 1807; Manifest
Destiny, phases of Reconstruction; various
ethnic, religious, racial, socio-economic groups
of people, etc.).

74FDA640261745A991BE2644EAABBC07.description:
Evaluate the extent to which a variety of
groups and individuals have had opportunity to
attain their perception of the “American
Dream” through Reconstruction (e.g., various
ethnic, religious, racial, socio-economic groups
of people; plantation society; transcendentalism; 49ers; etc.).

78802EA7AC644C028DD494FCAE854B5E.description:
Explain how opportunity and mobility
impacted various groups within American
society through Reconstruction (e.g., City on a
Hill, Lowell and other “mill towns”, Manifest
Destiny, immigrants/migrants, Gold Rush,
Homestead Act, Morrill Act, Exodusters,
women, various ethnic groups, etc.).

137F9CC815CB4CB3A14B8F6289B0C136.description:
Analyze the relationship between innovation,
economic development, progress and various
perceptions of the “American Dream” through
Reconstruction (e.g., inventions, Industrial
Revolution, American System, etc.).

8EECA4BCAA0A40B9B2CBBE1E52AF5D04.description:
Essential Standard: Analyze the
relationship between
progress, crisis and
the “American
Dream” within the
United States.

9CE0E6D0E8174EC58AE172D913A6FA41.description:
Explain the impact of wars on American
society and culture through Reconstruction
(e.g., salutary neglect, slavery, breakup of the
plantation system, carpetbaggers, scalawags,
KKK, and relocation of American Indians,
etc.).

69E3DA5952F14D909F5BC7913ECBF9E5.description:
Explain the impact of wars on the American
economy through Reconstruction (e.g.,
colonial debts, salutary neglect, protective
tariffs, inflation, profiteering, Hamilton’s
economic plan, embargo, American System,
Homesteaders, etc.).

3A63B70841324D8E878CFFF3B1744D42.description:
Explain the impact of wars on American
politics through Reconstruction (e.g., Issues of
taxation without representation, Proclamation
of 1763, Proclamation of Neutrality, XYZ Affair, Alien & Sedition Acts, War Hawks,
Hartford Convention, slavery Compromises,
scalawags, carpetbaggers, etc.).

906C481CBA19440187FA4469F3A91A62.description:
Essential Standard: Understand the
impact of war on
American politics,
economics, society and culture.

814ADE06B7314CADAD5E7F18470D4E76.description:
Explain the reasons for involvement in wars prior
to Reconstruction and the influence each
involvement had on international affairs (e.g.,
French and Indian War, War of 1812, Mexican
War, Civil War).

EEC40DFD08A24DC5B7F3326212EC2D50.description:
Explain how national economic and political
interests helped set the direction of United
States foreign policy from independence
through Reconstruction (e.g., treaties,
embargo, tariffs, Proclamation of Neutrality,
Monroe Doctrine, etc.).

ADFFA4B04A6F40C58D05B0894B3325FC.description:
Essential Standard: Understand how and
why the role of the
United States in the
world has changed
over time.

A412316B87704293A327DD016DCA280B.description:
Explain how judicial, legislative and executive
actions have affected the distribution of power
between levels of government from
colonization through Reconstruction (e.g., the
Marshall Court, Jacksonian era, nullification,
secession, etc.).

7F6EB7112C8B48EEAA99A0C337389835.description:
Summarize how the philosophical, ideological
and/or religious views on freedom and equality
contributed to the development of American
political and economic systems through
Reconstruction (e.g., natural rights, First Great
Awakening, Declaration of Independence,
transcendentalism, suffrage, abolition, “
slavery as a peculiar institution”, etc.).

3C99849CEDE24C18B86FF8C33494625F.description:
Essential Standard: Understand how
tensions between
freedom, equality and
power have shaped
the political,
economic and social
development of the
United States.

DCBA50C31EA041738F9A668865A5D175.description:
Analyze the cultural conflicts that impacted the
United States through Reconstruction and the
compromises that resulted (e.g., displacement
of American Indians, manifest destiny, slavery,
assimilation, nativism).

80C09437280641EEA4A5583442ACDA2F.description:
Analyze the social and religious conflicts,
movements and reforms that affected the
United States from colonization through
Reconstruction in terms of participants,
strategies, opposition, and results (e.g., Second
Great Awakening, Transcendentalism,
abolition, temperance, mental illness, prisons,
education, etc.).

C3401128F6084C5E946199A9D7AF7433.description:
Analyze the economic issues and conflicts that
impacted the United States through
Reconstruction and the compromises that
resulted (e.g., mercantilism, Revolutionary era
taxation, National Bank, taxes, tariffs,
territorial expansion, Economic “Panics”, Civil
War).

B00A7C85BA814791B8BEF134DDC1A3EE.description:
Analyze the political issues and conflicts that
impacted the United States through
Reconstruction and the compromises that
resulted (e.g., American Revolution,
Constitutional Convention, Bill of Rights,
development of political parties, nullification,
slavery, states’ rights, Civil War).

DCFC7238C6404B2A89C49E614EE160AD.description:
Essential Standard: Analyze how conflict
and compromise have
shaped politics,
economics and
culture in the United
States.

37CEDAA2EBC048E1A766C65B096AFA53.description:
Analyze voluntary and involuntary
immigration trends through Reconstruction in
terms of causes, regions of origin and
destination, cultural contributions, and public
and governmental response (e.g., Puritans, Pilgrims, American Indians, Quakers, ScotchIrish, Chinese, Africans, indentured servants,
slavery, Middle Passage, farming, ideas of the
Enlightenment, etc.).

49F586E22B374F54A27DF483B5A2DBFD.description:
Explain the roles of various racial and ethnic
groups in settlement and expansion through
Reconstruction and the consequences for those
groups (e.g., Germans, Scotch-Irish, Africans,
Native American Indians, Irish, Chinese, etc.).

FB1BDE48F5E34F569B2C9CD02FA41CEA.description:
Explain how environmental, cultural and
economic factors influenced the patterns of
migration and settlement within the U.S.
before the Civil War (e.g., economic diversity
of regions, mercantilism, cash crops, triangular
trade, ethnic diversity, Native American Indian
beliefs about land ownership, Lewis & Clark
expedition, farming, Industrial Revolution,
etc.).

E36B004634CC4D70ABFF5C0C599E785B.description:
Analyze how economic, political, social,
military and religious factors influenced
European exploration and American colonial
settlement (e.g., Reformation, mercantilism,
improvements in navigation technology,
colonization, defeat of Spanish Armada, Great
Awakening, etc.).

DDD030A170BB4E67B26813676F674C68.description:
Essential Standard: Understand the
factors that led to
exploration,
settlement,
movement, and
expansion and their
impact on United
States development
over time.

97CA38E22A0F43BD89571828F0AE372D.description:
Evaluate key turning points from colonization
through Reconstruction in terms of their
lasting impact (e.g., conflicts, legislation,
elections, innovations, leadership, movements,
Supreme Court decisions, etc.).

DCC8F00F6C654F52AD155457C1C41956.description:
Analyze key political, economic, and social
turning points from colonization through
Reconstruction in terms of causes and effects
(e.g., conflicts, legislation, elections,
innovations, leadership, movements, Supreme Court decisions, etc.)

4075AC31B16E4764840C2B14CCF4AFC0.description:
Essential Standard: Analyze key political,
economic and social
turning points in
American History
using historical

sources.
3. Support interpretations with historical
evidence.
4. Construct analytical essays using historical

701348490A594808813DE7882D65C560.description:

2. Consider multiple perspectives of various
peoples in the past.
3. Analyze cause-and-effect relationships and
multiple causation.
4. Evaluate competing historical narratives
and debates among historians.
5. Evaluate the influence of the past on
contemporary issues.

EEAF0D59CE4145D090C408A62B456B8C.description:
Use Historical Comprehension to:1. Reconstruct the literal meaning of a
historical passage.
2. Differentiate between historical facts and
historical interpretations.
3. Analyze data in historical maps.
4. Analyze visual, literary and musical
sources.

63FF1801F47D41CAB78B7A871741F02C.description:
Use Chronological thinking to:1. Identify the structure of a historical
narrative or story: (its beginning, middle
and end).
2. Interpret data presented in time lines and
create time lines.

53675CB742CE4EEE9A60E9D88C6D1DAA.description:
Essential Standard: Apply the four
interconnected
dimensions of
historical thinking to
the American History
Essential Standards
in order to
understand the
creation and
development of the
United States over
time.

literacy strategies.

● Differentiate between facts and interpretation of sources.
● Evaluate competing historical narratives and debates among historians.

communicate
conclusions and take
informed actions.

ABE3EE0CBE084F26AA313961A1B7361A.description:
Explain how movement and settlement patterns affected the development of
civilizations, empires, and societies in Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

9451F555FDF9447ABCC6841E0D90D7B5.description:
Explain how human and physical characteristics impacted migration and settlement in
various regions in Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.

E260AAC06EDA4FD396FAF580DAF73400.description: Understand the geographical factors that influence human migration and settlement.

6999C737D6A0492F84290D9753209504.description:
Explain the economic reasons for the rise and fall of civilizations, empires, and
societies in Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

2F31A49DEB934464A1B340EAA90D08B1.description:
Explain how trade routes and economic networks contribute to the development of
civilizations, empires, and classical societies in Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

44A67B9008D44707900D1CB7F2FA738C.description: Understand the economic activities of civilizations prior to 1400.

1A8076BCC3764B78A63479AE11504FD9.description:
Explain the reasons for the rise and fall of governments and authority in
civilizations and empires of Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

05E94A3A82D84D908489AEB1D791178C.description:
Summarize the beliefs and practices that shaped power and authority in various
civilizations, empires, and societies in Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.

0190B16C5053457CA3BBB2B77DC4C50A.description:
Compare the evolution of laws and legal systems in various civilizations, empires,
and societies in Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.

53EE437CD59747FB801F393C0B9DFAA3.description:
Compare the requirements for citizenship under various civilizations, empires,
and societies.

D0DEAB59144F4FF7A4808A0104F4B047.description: Compare how different types of government maintain power and authority.

76A8AEB85E8543A7AF675C5CE62FA26D.description:
Compare the structures of governmental systems in civilizations and societies in
Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.

A10A9A7B5F7B40BFAE5211F8B3A12841.description: Understand the purpose of government and authority.

C68FB60DFEB24ECFA112A2C6C6CF9099.description:
Compare systems of social structure within various civilizations and societies in Africa,
Asia, Europe and the Americas over time.

CCE9AF82650A4420B57156FBC2A8FD76.description:
Explain how artistic expressions reflect the values of civilizations in Africa, Asia,
Europe and the Americas.

A7C08461A8C147D5A950BAF96BEC990D.description:
Explain how religion, tradition, and cultural practice influence the development of
civilizations and societies in Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.

AAC2EE7837B343438F5EA54BA3A6E6D9.description: Understand ways in which culture influences civilizations.

83567848F9764BBEA335D297BF04BCFE.description: Use a range of civic approaches to address problems being investigated.

FBC8610C883240379785AE56B50E7BA8.description:
Identify challenges and opportunities created in addressing local, state, tribal, regional,
national, and/or global issues.

8826058088474BF3810DA21F850E0E97.description: Determine the credibility of disciplinary arguments of peers.

318052C678CD4603A07671C2EBF88FF1.description: Construct responses to supporting and opposing perspectives supported by evidence.

7235DAB094D14AAC93ABF117FEE8F87B.description:
Construct arguments consisting of multiple claims with evidence from sources and
attention to disciplinary detail.

FA09A5DBDD7F4A5BBA759BA4FE3A5D90.description:
Construct claims and counterclaims using evidence while pointing out the strengths
and limitations of both based on multiple sources.

E291CF9479854AC6A6CF357C1E80BEE9.description: Identify evidence that draws information from multiple perspectives.

0ECDF8893CD74AD88E43294BB6158017.description:
Assess the credibility of primary and secondary sources using the origin, authority,
structure, credibility, reliability, and context of the sources to guide the selection.

D89FE05C68344828A12B495D8969844D.description:
Analyze details, central ideas, and inferences from sources using discipline-specific
strategies.

D622E82EAB6642FDA886A2D6076C24ED.description: Construct supporting questions based upon disciplinary concepts.

5ED6793A0AE440ADB759E18133B54C4F.description: Construct a compelling question through a disciplinary lens individually and with peers.

document.title: NORTH CAROLINA STANDARD COURSE OF STUDY  K-12 Science, Biology

071821EB352C4E848FA5E03EF7632AB0.description:
Use models (including dichotomous keys, scientific nomenclature,
cladograms, phylogenetic trees) to identify organisms and exemplify relationships.

9911C2F8A0674009B9F6EAB3D3F5845F.description:
Construct explanations to illustrate how varying environmental conditions
may result in: changes in the number of individuals of a species, the emergence of
new species over time, or the extinction of other species.

4A9DD62384464CAF8CEA5FE35204B135.description:
Construct an explanation to explain how natural selection leads to
adaptations within populations.

E59DE35600EA42C49D6AB5C522C08C3E.description:
Use models to illustrate the conditions required for natural selection,
including the overproduction of offspring, inherited variation, and the struggle to
survive.

8F4977D7822F47DD93FE6031D3E10F12.description:
Construct an explanation to illustrate how common ancestry and biological
evolution are supported by multiple lines of empirical evidence.

73A97E3287154B1AB1BBBFDCEC351D6D.description:
Analyze and interpret data to summarize how various factors such as
geographic isolation, pesticide resistance, antibiotic resistance can influence natural
selection.

C1DE02AE821741048A0F1E57C2159362.description:
Understand natural
selection as a mechanism for
biological evolution.

F8052B34AF6D4C26B82ECA3D05DED2B0.description:
Obtain and communicate information that summarizes the impact of
biotechnology applications on the individual, society, and the environment, including
agriculture and medicine.

154DA8E90ACE4CCD980791BDD912B3C5.description: Analyze and interpret data to compare DNA samples.

DEB6861CA09140DA8C5BD76691745A10.description:
Understand
applications of genetics and
biotechnology.

2B3E0BDBBFAD4D63A0FD8372B78D17F8.description:
Construct an explanation to summarize how traits result from interactions
of genetic factors (multiple genes and/or alleles) and environmental factors.

D68622A70C36408E92A147EDB30857FD.description:
Analyze and interpret data to explain how polygenic traits result in a wide
range of phenotypes.

DEA3C86670E2430C99AF906D3F60BF1B.description:
Use mathematics and computational thinking to predict the variation and
distribution of expressed traits based on: Mendelian inheritance, co-dominance,
incomplete dominance, multiple alleles, and sex-linked inheritance.

5E8F8330CADA4ADCA11CC86A0E5247F9.description:
Understand types of
inheritance and how the
environment can influence
traits.

E749F32948604D35941E44B80745EB60.description:
Construct an explanation to summarize how inheritable genetic variations
may result from: new genetic combinations in meiosis,mutations during replication, or
mutations caused by environmental factors.

D270C60699104A94834EE3362E8DC6FB.description:
Use models to explain how DNA is passed from parents to offspring
through the processes of meiosis and fertilization in sexual reproduction.

7352B41038F34F1E800246D4ED193D61.description: Heredity- Inheritance and Variation of Traits

F64C3874C69742F5BABCFD31FDC51350.description:
Engage in argument from evidence to evaluate various solutions to
reduce the impact of human activities on biodiversity and ecosystem health.

86DB726A0E6641B3B00DEBC56951E0B2.description:
Use mathematics and computational thinking to explain how interactions
between organisms (predator/prey, competition) affect carrying capacity and maintain
stability in an ecosystem.

760C71D0D39746F88AC204C33C072C7D.description:
Understand
ecosystem dynamics,
functioning, and resilience.

052C4550BA13411DAABF20FF9850F20E.description:
Use models to explain the relationship between the flow of energy and
cycling of matter among organisms in an ecosystem.

33A85F7AF9C54F54BCB08F7A5AF10FEA.description:
Use models to illustrate how processes in organisms contribute to the flow
of energy and the cycling of matter within an ecosystem.

F375D720BD5E4D648D232AB74EF9E5D3.description:
Analyze the
relationships between matter
and energy within
ecosystems.

58740BDACADB4E5FAA725A67A58210E9.description:
Use models to illustrate how cellular respiration [aerobic and anaerobic]
transforms chemical energy into ATP.

A94F6E8B43784E3A9453D6926CA28186.description:
Use models to illustrate how photosynthesis transforms light energy into
chemical energy.

D93A5501A5E84001A18ACDF58B10C969.description:
Carry out investigations to explain how homeostasis is maintained through
feedback mechanisms.

0404E72F0B5C49A99FB3F2CA03CFCCC7.description:
Analyze the
relationship between
biochemical processes and
energy use.

514662CACC0F4F2FBD5856D031E0178E.description:
Construct an explanation to illustrate that proteins regulate gene
expression resulting in cellular differentiation, specialized cells with specific functions,
and uncontrolled cell growth.

81109BC50A0248FC87D11CC015639EC7.description:
Use models to illustrate how cellular division results in the reproduction,
growth, and repair of organisms.

E093D8BB797446B6BDB36627B7A8950B.description:
Analyze the growth
and development processes
of organisms.

A800E8DFE9304E028B15E7AAC54ADD13.description:
Construct an explanation to summarize how DNA and RNA direct the
synthesis of proteins.

C21FA323DA1049CF95BE62788E60D8F3.description:
Construct explanations to compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells in
terms of structures and degree of complexity.

418D351A96BD44499C45DB8BD3E947D0.description:
Use models to explain how the structure of organelles determines its
function and supports overall cell processes.

5B7460E62C9A4A37A3B29E7835004498.description:
Carry out investigations to illustrate how enzymes act as catalysts for
biochemical reactions and how environmental factors affect enzyme activity.

3DDCCC3CA5D4454CAC244F285890D404.description:
Construct an explanation to illustrate relationships between structure and
function of major macromolecules essential for life.

34CF07ECF8B14F8DBB434792A13482D3.description:
Analyze how the
relationship between
structure and function
supports life processes within
organisms.

648B86A39C764539B4609B56E2A02EC4.description: From Molecules to Organisms- Structures and Processes

standardSets.title: Cognitive Development (CD)

document.title: North Carolina Foundations for Early Learning and Development

C7893A0F30534887860A56254E41B534.description:
Manipulate the environment to
produce desired effects and invent
solutions to problems (attach a piece
of string to the light switch so they can
independently turn off the lights).

B6C3110AB29B4ADCACA146D3B27BC0FF.description:
Make and check predictions through
observations and experimentation,
with adult support and guidance.

D7EC843018B949A9907139510E88E09B.description:
Use an increasing variety of tools to
investigate the world around them
(measuring tools, balance, prism,
droppers).

9917D22D125749CAAFE79AD5E06816EA.description:
Compare objects, materials,
and phenomena by observing
and describing their physical
characteristics.

218DFAC475AD43C7BDCA1565D7BD2281.description:
Ask questions and identify ways to
find answers (look in a book, use the
computer, try something and watch
what happens).

76FEEE30FE464B17AFACFEE4A1F75234.description:
Represent what they learn during
scientific exploration through drawing,
modeling, building, movement, or
other methods.

49BA2CDD3DCC42BAA26E7201BD3A43E1.description:
Describe and predict
changes that take
place when mixing and
manipulating materials.

9254000514B14994A5FF08F85DEDFB0A.description:
Use simple tools to
investigate objects and
materials, with guidance
and support (magnifying
glass, sifter, ramps for
rolling balls and cars).

4AAF24BE99944AD1A6E40E125D291CF3.description:
Ask questions to find out
more about the natural
world.

61E95D757E7841A9943FB171AECEE829.description:
Observe objects,
materials, and
phenomena and
describe what they notice
(temperature, texture,
size, weight, color, etc.).

12DE3964D75C4C3E838E117110EF9D17.description:
Represent what they
learn during scientific
exploration through
drawing, modeling,
building, movement, or
other methods.

CF52818607D64685A541A84F4F67AD0B.description:
Children explore the world by observing, manipulating objects,
asking questions, making predictions, and developing generalizations.

45D03AD779EB4E46BB36EC87A8601982.description:
Participate in activities that help to care
for the environment and explain why they
are important with guidance and support
(gathering cans for recycling, planting
trees).

5841B389DD4E48FCB44726D6DD176CBC.description:
Notice, describe, and attempt to explain
properties of materials and changes in
substances (metal railing is hot because
the sun shines on it; ice melts when it gets
warmer).

4A6BF392E80F403FB30D79621E4CB653.description:
Notice and describe weather conditions,
position of the sun and moon at different
times, and seasonal changes.

4307D766ADFA4086921A4AC79B26C5E8.description:
Take responsibility for the care of living
things (independently feed classroom pet
as daily chore, water plant when dry, weed
vegetable garden).

347FF3F91AA846C1AE8299B5CB951CEF.description:
Describe some things plants and animals need
to live and grow (sunlight, water, food).

129EB42F3FF34B609272C7A28ED283A8.description:
Notice and react to the natural world and
the outdoor environment.

BF73F863CA79499FB30C17236C492940.description:
Collect items from nature (rocks, leaves,
insects) and classify them using physical
characteristics (color, size, shape, texture).

77484A60332240CC82486CEF05226F6E.description:
Participate in activities that help
to care for the environment,
with guidance and support
(pick up trash, recycle paper).

DD14BA70E69B44FF9CCCD851C264D54A.description:
Notice and describe properties
of materials and changes in
substances (water freezes into
ice, pudding thickens, clay
hardens).

1B51D4DA6D5F40A9A6C0A44E6C37E46F.description:
Notice and describe current
weather conditions.

75F407E179B24259BD660AA3C2245B20.description:
Notice and describe
characteristics of plants and
animals, such as appearance,
similarities, differences,
behavior, and habitat.

2059A09269B54621A5C42EA0AE94E1E9.description:
Notice and react to the natural
world and the outdoor
environment.

1D0ED52BF5F0471FA2E6B59463B60224.description:
Participate in the care of living
things, with guidance and
support (water plants, help to
feed classroom pet).

554956EBFA37455DA2C33D3372A33689.description:
Children observe and describe characteristics of living things
and the physical world.

8F67C96AB82D404594CF030320945D6B.description:
Begin to explain how a mathematical
problem was solved (“I saw that
there was always a blue flower after
a red flower so I knew to put a blue
one next.” “I counted four friends
who didn’t have cookies so I got four
more.”).

058C0E3A9EAA42889053B7118B157F17.description:
Use drawing and concrete materials
to represent an increasing variety
of mathematical ideas (draw
shapes to represent pattern; stack
different-colored blocks to represent
classmates’ answers to a survey
question).

D683CB3B8BDB42E6852EA85CDEC14FBF.description:
Use observation and counting with
increasing accuracy to answer
questions such as “How many do
we need?” and “How many more
do we need?” during play and other
daily activities (count new children
to see how many more plates are
needed for snack; return extra drinks
to cooler at picnic to arrive at the
correct number).

CFCDA4435375446CB918BB214A3E6298.description:
Seek answers to questions during
play and daily activities using an
increasing variety of mathematical
strategies.

D568B2B357E747F4A7826F7155B30622.description:
Use drawing and concrete
materials to represent
mathematical ideas (draw many
circles to show “lots of people,”
put Popsicle® sticks in a pile to
show the number of children who
want crackers for snack).

3AC465B134DC498B8BC026592E66FC00.description:
Use observation and counting
(not always correctly) to find out
how many things are needed
during play and other daily
activities (figure out how many
spoons are needed for snack,
find enough dolls so each person
has one when playing in the
dramatic play area).

CDD55D79AB8F4546B33667EBA9B7155D.description:
Seek answers to questions by
using mathematical thinking
during play and daily activities
(determine who is taller by
standing next to classmate; find
two smaller blocks to replace
larger block).

155D84039C3F496DA9EE2EAD62566257.description:
Children use mathematical thinking to solve problems
in their everyday environment.

DFDCDE738F1547A88D074654C3EAD144.description:
Name basic shapes
and describe their
characteristics using
descriptive and geometric
attributes (“That’s a
triangle; it’s pointy.” “It’s a
circle because it’s round.”).

36B6B6EB9ED84A5AA0CB5634E01A7EB6.description:
Use 2- and 3-dimensional
shapes to represent realworld objects (say, “We are
building a castle and we
need a round block for the
tunnel.” “I glued a circle
and a square on my picture
to make a house.”).

BD9704C6A97D4176B932663B4FBFAD97.description:
Consistently use a variety
of words for positions
in space, and follow
directions using these
words.

53946ECA95F449139D28D7F6C367A1C4.description:
Find shapes in the
environment and describe
them in their own words.

17902028C4244F67ADEC14AB459BFFE6.description:
Use 2- and 3-dimensional
shapes to create pictures,
designs, or structures.

55A846CC39D44289AF47EEE462CD335D.description:
Show they understand
positions in space by
using position words
during play and by
following directions from
an adult (say, “Stand
behind the chair.” “Put the
ball in the box.”).

E1DDF73A99044F53A5F2D6EE04956F83.description:
Children identify and use common shapes and concepts about position
during play and other activities.

61A1C0E8FDDC4C799B1341DCF588CD5B.description:
Duplicate and extend simple patterns
using concrete objects (look at a
pattern of beads and tell what bead
comes next in the pattern).

F76E02D426D14BE3A81DEEFEBCA6A302.description:
Sort a group of objects (0-10) using
one attribute (color, size, shape,
quantity) with increasing accuracy
(sort blocks by shape and place
like-shaped blocks on the shelf; sort
beads by color).

3A22A449E1FD45F7BDFD69D4BCD899F1.description:
Put a few objects in order by length (arrange a group of 3 blocks in order from
the shortest to the longest).

0E22A18276D34242BFC1D552BB2BE134.description:
Directly compare more than two
objects by size, length, or weight
(“That rock is heavier than these
others; I can’t lift it.” Look at three
strings that are different lengths and
select the longest string).

5AB924C4ECD048D284C9AB683CDF497E.description:
Use simple measurement tools with
guidance and support to measure
objects (a ruler, measuring cup,
scale).

6DC882D7D12949C0A0AFB6567521872C.description:
Use descriptive language for size,
length, or weight (short, tall, long,
heavy, big).

8E7670BADDBD414F81940783AECA0CD5.description:
Recognize simple repeating patterns
and attempt to create them during
play (repeat a movement pattern
during a song, make a line of blocks
in alternating colors).

9359DA4BF5D042DEBC752903411E0A67.description:
Sort familiar objects into categories
with increasing accuracy (tools
for woodworking and utensils for
cooking; rectangle blocks on one
shelf and square blocks on another
shelf).

9504CBA4867E438A8ACD082844F72DF4.description:
Identify familiar objects as the same
or different.

671C9357B37F4E609202C7C06A552308.description:
Compare the size or weight of two
objects and identify which one is longer/
taller/heavier than the other (“That rock
is heavier than this one; I can’t lift it.” “A
snake is longer than a worm.”).

274CFCF5E8594F9888EB9D3FC32EA7C1.description:
Use simple measurement tools with
guidance and support to measure
objects (a ruler, measuring cup,
scale).

A9EE5739E92B4122A391AE5C249047D1.description:
Use descriptive language for size,
length, or weight (short, tall, long,
heavy, big).

F48065E5D028461194137AFD5C5544E4.description:
Children compare, sort, group, organize and measure objects and create patterns
in their everyday environment.

0ED4C9F11D614DDE8797B6BF03F4435B.description:
Show understanding of first, next,
and last during play and daily
activities (answer questions about
who is first and last to slide down
the slide; say, “The engine is first,
and the caboose is last” when
making a train).

42F8773CF65C4A228C5B60A9C005007D.description:
Recognize some numerals and
attempt to write them during play
and daily activities.

493199E9779346D9B5581BDC20BC74D6.description:
Match numerals 1-5 to sets of
objects, with guidance and
support.

80552DF396C84B41BBC6ECEC648CC204.description:
Write numerals or number-like
forms during play and daily
activities.

516B79DB042F470EBA82140F1E9A7E27.description:
Show they understand that putting
two groups of objects together
will make a bigger group and that
a group of objects can be taken
apart into smaller groups.

9AD43440D4CA40DD987888BEC0E2CAEA.description:
Show they understand that
adding objects to a group
will make a bigger group,
and taking away objects
will make a smaller group.

75650F7A3DF543769E2EF085E6B2D909.description:
Children show understanding of numbers and quantities
during play and other activities.

36AE08A3354648DCBC47FCC28447479B.description:
Compare the amount of items
in small sets of objects (up to 5
objects) by matching or counting
and use language such as “more
than” and “less than” to describe
the sets of objects.

B430A0CCA8D44210A184B553A5077648.description:
Given a number 0-5, count out
that many objects.

4E7D014B0736477ABB50882799FF325B.description:
Count up to 10 objects arranged
in a line using one-to-one
correspondence with increasing
accuracy, and answer the
question “How many?”

1F0A44A262D84A999A62C19882903DCA.description:
Without counting, state the
number of objects in a small
collection (1-3) (when a friend
holds up two fingers, look at
her hand and say, “Two fingers”
without counting).

314E6954C5764A908D5455E4F987F5C0.description:
Rote count in order to 20 with
increasing accuracy.

FC8DC7D190B74D5D93EDC5C114C1DE46.description:
Compare visually two
groups of objects that
are obviously equal or
unequal in quantity and
communicate that they
are the same or different,
and which one has more
(choose a plate with four
cookies rather than a plate
with one cookie).

953798FAEA194E7B9DDB64CEF2810AB0.description:
Count up to 5 objects
arranged in a line
using one-to-one
correspondence with
increasing accuracy, and
answer the question “How
many?”

EF11489681CD4783B6CDDFF1FF0A4C02.description:
Rote count in order to 10
with increasing accuracy.

8A140203520C4AF793CEF5A62CC5383C.description:
Children show understanding of numbers and quantities
during play and other activities.

AACDE03BE2BD405180A3B66F56464C79.description:
Demonstrate positive social behaviors
and take personal responsibility as a
member of a group (share, take turns,
follow rules, take responsibility for
classroom jobs).

9A3DFF202F95412C8104DE10940B8366.description:
Show awareness of the basic needs all
families have (food, shelter, clothing)
and how needs are met (work, help
each other).

9A1A36E35DD64739AA030CBF3FCB5828.description:
Observe and talk about how people
adapt to seasons and weather
conditions (put out salt in icy weather,
wear rain gear).

4F8182ADDE7B4064B66EC02E7C0CE52D.description:
Observe and talk about changes in
themselves and their families over time.

54D64FF738A2406CB7A3ACF0E8177836.description:
Describe characteristics of the places
where they live and play (say, “My house
is big and there are trees in my yard.”
“The playground has swings and a
sandbox.”).

65C1066F993146A1836BAAAA796B1F56.description:
With prompting and
support, participate as a
member of a democratic
classroom community (vote
for name of class pet, wait
turn to paint when easels
are full).

E75DCAF18F8246799A5A51B5CC96092E.description:
Notice and talk about
weather conditions.

3E9DD2B7331C4173A084F915E248E106.description:
Notice changes that
happen over time (seasons,
self or others growing
bigger).

2F11EE2EC9F04C92A89A9037FAA6B70E.description:
Describe characteristics
of the places where they
live and play (say, “My
house is big and there are
trees in my yard.” “The
playground has swings and
a sandbox.”).

1102816C1B6C455791986CC62BF9D94B.description:
Children explore concepts connected with their daily experiences
in their community.

47CD6B6A5F8D4AD3A88E82F7422AF994.description:
Show acceptance of
different cultures through
exploration of varying
customs and traditions,
past and present (how
people dress, how
people speak, food,
music, art, etc.).

D65ADB39F7CC4368BA25E5B25AAEF2A2.description:
Talk about how other
children have different
family members and
family structures than
their own (“I live with my
Grandma and Shanika
lives with her Mom and
Dad.” “David’s dad works
but my Daddy stays
home and takes care of
me.”).

B14E3E1B07BE4523B2E8A38CC734C95F.description:
Show acceptance of
people who are different
from themselves as

document.title: Holocaust and Genocide Studies - Course Objectives

Classify misinformation and disinformation related to Holocaust distortion
and denial.

contemporary societies.

Holocaust.

Compare the differing interpretations in the study of the Holocaust by
German and American historians.

037FB8CFD5FC4AFFBAC503E0D6918F05.description:
Describe the resilience of Holocaust survivors to Nazism, antisemitism, and
discrimination from 1933 to the present day.

2A9F3454B1C24C2B84ECDD554CFE944F.description:
Explain the impact of stolen goods on Jewish heritage, history, and
survivors.

668192D678FD44BD8C9B185E3D02B163.description:
Summarize the importance of museums, monuments, and memorials in
commemorating the Holocaust and preserving its historical record.

8E53CDBE84F34D90854C3571CA5495DE.description:
Describe the challenges survivors faced in rebuilding their lives after the
Holocaust.

63C8986D223647B8877668CADEA6AD0A.description:
Summarize the success of post-war efforts in prosecuting perpetrators of
crimes of Nazism.

B7CF3128D591424384E460DB7754F5BD.description:
Explain the establishment of the State of Israel and its influence on Jewish
immigration after World War II.

59FF3EE8DEB4492BA618D476A23264A8.description:
Use primary and secondary sources to help demonstrate ways in which the
Allies used the Nuremberg Trials to expose crimes against victims of the Holocaust.

FDB00E495CB54B718A63FAC144F29B51.description:
Explain how stereotypes, propaganda, and isolationist policies impacted
immigration laws and policies around the world regarding Jews and others targeted by
the Nazis.

C2E00A85269E423A8AAB5325005D8802.description: Differentiate significant global responses to the Holocaust during and after WWII.

B0C3D9643A864154ADC55A4EBF5EF9B3.description: Global Responses to the Holocaust: Before, During, & After

14E97874D6E04916A99108759E6FB9F4.description:
Distinguish ways in which various forms of resistance can be seen as a
means to preserve Jewish identity and culture for survivors of the Holocaust.

F361D2866E794ACE85D7368AC9C1BCA2.description:
Explain how acts of resistance by Jews, non-Jews, the youth, women, and
formal resistance forces contributed to prolonging or ensuring the survival of those
targeted by the Nazis.

ED652CFD16324F8D9AB293CFE67B64F2.description:
Describe various survival and resistance strategies used by men, women,
and children in the camps and ghettos.

E60A7AEEACAA4144B2184014FE82DBF0.description:
Use primary source evidence such as artifacts, survivor testimony, and diary
entries to describe the challenges of life in the various camps and ghettos of Germanoccupied territories.

177F00A2C9B342B1896955F7DF0D8D26.description:
Explain how the Nazi infrastructure of transportation and other bureaucratic
systems were used to enable the deportation and annihilation of Jewish people and
other enemies of the state.

AAE82FA086EB48969F94CA779F9AD6EB.description: Describe life in different types of camps.

635FE7CCC1D141A0871D6C40784241D9.description: Categorize Nazi camps by type, purpose, and kind of prisoners.

CEE1B208EABE4CB6B410A2FE19DBCBCE.description:
Explain the reasoning for the creation of ghettos under the Nazi regime and
how they functioned.

08DABB3EEE2947CEB553A0DF3ED0DD87.description: Jewish Life in Europe After Hitler’s Rise to Power

3A9258B12B224923B6C17E1E80DFCFCF.description:
Describe the various ways in which the Nazis executed the Final Solution;
and the effects.

6D284E55AD6A45F7B78067E78749B0EE.description:
Compare the actions of both the United States and Germany at the outset
of WWII in terms of how government actions impacted the lives of citizens.

7C3A3A63FDA14A7B9313542AC06EE671.description: Explain how the events of World War II and the Holocaust are connected.

C25F1511C27B4E5C80B2D6E7AB79AC27.description:
Describe the various forms of resistance, in Germany and Nazi-occupied
territories, to the Nazi regimentation of society.

5578AB7623B14633B256768A0B8C160F.description:
Compare how media outlets in different parts of the world reported on the
Nazi regime, persecution of Jews, and the Holocaust before and after the outbreak of
war.

D680E3791D9343BBBF1BA76C78738EF9.description:
Use primary and secondary sources to determine what governments and
citizens around the world knew about the mass murder of Jews during World War II.

D76FE316D742452D84F1390C24AD392E.description:
Describe the role that perpetrators, collaborators, bystanders, resisters, and
rescuers played before, during, and after the Holocaust.

8B6E3C35113F41F7B1614659075553C0.description:
Explain the causes and effects of key turning points on Jews in Germany
and Nazi-controlled territories, 1937-1941.

779124AB0B224FC28CAD1F3B2F119CB2.description:
Summarize the opportunities and challenges involved in emigration from
Nazi-controlled areas of Europe.

B6D1482B13714DF7BBAD13D4A023C940.description:
Identify the individuals, groups, and nations that served as allies of the Nazi
regime and the reasons for their alliance with the Nazis.

F390B4AFBA2C4B43B69DAF6A673F83D0.description: Define the Holocaust according to the "Never Again Education Act".

A301C7AD040C4357B42BAFC9547BC094.description:
Describe how the Nazis used euphemisms to disguise their actions against
Jews and those considered political enemies of the state.

A60795032C9B4ECCB710E51CE10E5735.description: Explain how Nazi ideology impacted the behavior of individuals and groups.

92BF9BB79A9C445598E6FB5486D7D55A.description:
Describe the Nazi motivations for racial purity and the various ways they
tried to secure a pure “Aryan” race.

8E7EA9CFD2964F849FC6AEE376C024E5.description:
Describe Nazi policies and laws from 1933-1938 in terms of their ability to
consolidate power, disenfranchise, and separate groups from society.

1AA7D054CEAD4D73B1BEBEA07C8F71D9.description:
Describe the role of propaganda, conspiracy theories, and the media in
promoting Nazi ideology.

283009CB995C449F903A39F90188A7B0.description:
Identify the various groups the Nazis targeted for state-sponsored
persecution.

C182155CBCA840229E93138723B11439.description:
Distinguish the connections between Social Darwinism, Lebensraum,
euthanasia, eugenics, and America's concept of Manifest Destiny.

62A7B52935A343BD9A7EA0C4EF2EBAAD.description:
Summarize how German nationalism and the rise of Hitler were influenced
by both historical and cultural factors.

32C935C2FA8C450CAF91BDAEFA599099.description:
Describe the diverse range of Jewish culture, tradition, and experiences
prior to the Holocaust.

could use to respond to various stages of genocide.

E9A68AFCA1B447929CDC942D0A3B2E4B.description:
Compare the motivations for and effects of international responses to various
genocides of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries.

BFCC43B4742346238F79D2843983FAEF.description: Identify genocides of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries.

35E12EE1660043EE97538B0B6ED17F7A.description: Define genocide according to the United Nations.

Explain how prejudice, stereotypes, stereotypes, bias, scapegoating, and
discrimination contributed to the Holocaust and global responses to the Holocaust.

Explain how the Nazi Party gained popularity using antisemitism and
presenting Jews as the source of political, economic, and social problems of pre-WWII
Germany.

DEC0FABFBBFD4ED584362CA5FAAA182C.description:
Analyze art, propaganda, symbols, and other forms of communication to
draw comparisons across eras on the beliefs and behaviors associated with
antisemitism.

1AE77DF476884E759890B9D53ED1F2EF.description:
Explain the impact of antisemitism and its tenets, on groups and societies
from ancient times through the twenty-first century.

E33A962E8A8646B49DCDFB33C88BE39C.description:
Distinguish different forms of antisemitism and how they have impacted
Jewish communities throughout history, including modern-day manifestations.

15FB8F6EAD484A8E9F6F536ABC4EC0A0.description:
Summarize the history of relations between Jews and non-Jews in European
societies leading up to the Holocaust.

CBE86AD739FE4E7B8CCD28A9596EBB7A.description: Define antisemitism according to the "Never Again Education Act".

2AC48B94B2F84C7FB62C7B33C04AF4F0.description:
Use geographic tools to describe and visualize the geography of the
Holocaust.

B05F59BDB7AD4B2C80A67FF0181CC717.description:
Interpret data presented in charts, graphs, tables, and timelines to place the
events of the Holocaust in a historical and comparative context.

0CE532DA40E241728A4A9F18EF5FDE3D.description:
Summarize how stereotyping and bias contribute to the misinterpretation
and denial of the complex history of the Holocaust.

7CB9E2C4E3FF4623B16C5DED17EC2C29.description:
Analyze multiple perspectives of individuals and groups through the practice
of historical empathy by examining differing motives, beliefs, actions, and desired
outcomes.

341697A342B340AC89323D5EA29614BD.description:
Analyze historical perspectives describing the Holocaust or other genocides
through the eyes and experiences of those who were there, as revealed through
literature, diaries, letters, debates, arts, artifacts, etc.

terms of origin, authority, reliability, literary significance, and context.
